Measured, not landed (experiment reverted). Rule tried in SourceBundle.validate: every stream's native axis is the primary axis or an axis named by one of the bundle's mappings. It admits the real composed Sherlock bundle (SherlockSourceAtlas: part streams keep their part axes and each has a TrackComposition) and refuses the borrowed-axis bundle. coreJVM+storyJVM+codecJVM+documentJVM: 257 run, 12 failed, all in core (D1bPointSupportSuite x1, D1aSupportSuite x11): those fixtures deliberately build a secondary stream on its own unmapped axis (here another film's primary axis, used as a convenient clock) and add mappings later. So the D1a model admits unmapped secondary native axes by design; the strict rule is a source-model change, not a narrow fix.
Options for the owner:
(a) Strict mapping rule above; rebuild 12 D1a fixtures to declare mappings; an unaligned secondary stream becomes unrepresentable.
(b) Axis ownership: a stream's native axis is either the primary axis, a per-stream content-addressed axis (cannot coincide with another bundle's axis), or a mapped foreign axis. Core API change, ADR needed.
(c) Leave core; every consumer that treats equal axes as the same footage also compares bundles (document done at 9252b8129). Needs a survey of align (temporalsupport, mappingsource), corpus-intake and codec.
Recommendation: (c) now with the survey, (b) as the durable fix via ADR.
